dialogue.speaker: William
dialogue.text: Finally… Nothing beats the end of working day

dialogue.speaker: William
dialogue.text: Why is there a letter from… that place anyways?

dialogue.speaker: Narration
dialogue.text: I hope this letter reaches you and you didn’t immediately throw it away. Do read it first, I don’t plan to ask much from you nor to cause any trouble. You don’t have to know who I am. I’m merely curious about how the city has been treating you these days.

dialogue.speaker: Narration
dialogue.text: The city is heaven, isn't it? Lots of opportunities. Plenty of possibilities. Even fresh chances to achieve your deep-rooted dreams. Still, you realize it, don’t you? That no matter how far you run from the woods, you know that…

dialogue.speaker: Narration
dialogue.text: Only the worthy ones deserve heaven.

dialogue.speaker: Narration
dialogue.text: The doors will greet you with open arms.

dialogue.speaker: Narration
dialogue.text: If you walk through the woods to the place that was once your home now, you’ll see the walls are as steady as ever, expected from the Blackwoods. The roofs are still looming high to the sky though the power is now weak. The crickets still sing their ode late into the night.

dialogue.speaker: Narration
dialogue.text: Nobody lives there anymore. Nobody comes by.

dialogue.speaker: Narration
dialogue.text: I hope you can do me a favor to visit the manor again. Though I can’t guarantee that we will meet there, but you won’t be alone.

dialogue.speaker: William
dialogue.text: “Only the worthy ones deserve heaven”... Who even knows that?

dialogue.speaker: William (thoughts)
dialogue.text: Who even sent this invitation to me after all these years?

dialogue.speaker: William (thoughts)
dialogue.text: Ignoring the invitation does feel kind of rude, though

dialogue.speaker: William
dialogue.text: Let’s get this over with, then…
